name: Syndromic Respiratory or Mediastinal Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Syndromic Respiratory or Mediastinal Malformation Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural malformation affecting the respiratory tract or mediastinum
Presence of additional syndromic features such as craniofacial dysmorphism or limb anomalies
Radiological evidence of mediastinal or respiratory tract malformation on CT or MRI
Identification of pathogenic variant in known associated gene(s) if available
Exclusion of acquired or isolated respiratory malformations without syndromic association

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including congenital respiratory or mediastinal malformation and syndromic features, supported by imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory due to heterogeneity

searchTerms: trachea or bronchus stenosis present at birth
mass or cyst in chest area

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to airway obstruction
searchTerms: feeding problems due to blocked airway
poor feeding caused by airway issues

occasional.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to airway malformation
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from airway issues
pulmonary hypertension due to airway defects
lung blood vessel pressure rise from malformations
growth and learning delays due to hypoxia
developmental problems linked to oxygen deficiency

rare.symptomName: Cardiac malformations associated with mediastinal anomalies
searchTerms: cardiac malformations linked to mediastinal issues
heart problems associated with chest masses
weak immune system from small thymus
immune deficiency due to thymic underdevelopment

rare.symptomName: Hematological abnormalities secondary to syndromic involvement
searchTerms: hematologic problems related to genetic disorders
blood cell issues secondary to syndromic disease

laboratory: Possible lymphopenia in cases with thymic hypoplasia
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: CT or MRI showing tracheobronchial malformations or mediastinal cystic lesions
Chest X-ray revealing mediastinal shift or mass
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes associated with syndromic respiratory malformations (e.g., TBX1, FOXF1)
other: Bronchoscopy demonstrating airway stenosis or malformation
Echocardiography to assess associated cardiac anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Localized cystic lesion without syndromic association

redFlags: Severe airway obstruction causing respiratory distress
Rapidly enlarging mediastinal mass compromising cardiovascular function
